rows.verified: Employers must assess welding activities and identify measures needed to control exposure to welding fume.
Exposure should first be avoided or reduced by changing the process, reducing welding or using lower-fume methods and materials.
Suitable local exhaust ventilation should capture welding fume at source where reasonably practicable.
Respiratory protective equipment is required where local exhaust ventilation alone does not adequately control exposure.
Outdoor welding generally requires suitable respiratory protection because local exhaust ventilation is not effective outdoors.
Exposure-control equipment should be checked for damage, kept in working order and repaired promptly when faulty.
Local exhaust ventilation should be thoroughly examined and tested by a competent person at least every 14 months.
Respiratory health surveillance should be provided where the risk assessment identifies a reasonable likelihood of welding-related asthma or disease.
The required controls depend on welding process, metal, coating, duration, location, ventilation and nearby workers.
Welding-fume evidence is process- and exposure-specific and is not an exact parcel-level respiratory-risk probability.
Respirable crystalline silica is fine dust generated when silica-containing materials such as stone, brick, concrete and mortar are cut or worked.
Respirable crystalline silica can penetrate deep into the lungs and cause serious disease.
COSHH requires employers and self-employed people to control exposure to respirable crystalline silica.
Construction tasks should follow an Assess, Control and Review approach to dust risk.
High-dust tasks such as concrete grinding or scabbling require effective engineering controls.
Dust generation should be reduced before work starts by design, material selection and lower-dust work methods.
On-tool extraction and water suppression are recognised controls for many silica-generating tasks.
Health surveillance must be considered where workers are regularly exposed and there is a reasonable likelihood of silicosis developing.
Actual exposure depends on material silica content, task, duration, enclosure, extraction performance, housekeeping and respiratory protection.
Silica evidence is material-, task- and exposure-specific and is not an exact parcel-level respiratory-risk probability.
